_readme: FROM THE IMPACT TO THE SHORE IN ONE TAKE (2026-10-25, Mark: "like the orbit one but two minutes, the orbit
going all the way down to a bird's eye view following the waves crashing onto land"). A 1 km impactor
(1950 DA's class) at 20 km/s into 35 N 42 W at the scene's start, on ONE clock at 170x: the front reaches
the Merrimack's mouth 3.68 h after the impact at 78 s of the 120 s record, the train's peak near 5 h at
106 s, and the eye is over the inlet from 80 s on, 3 km over Plum Island at the end as the water comes
up the creeks and over the marsh. The solver's window is on, its faces fed by the wave's level; the wave
solve keeps its first read of the solver's current. The drawn far wave is 10x (on the deep wave before
the shoaling's bound); the solver's water is raw.
Why 1 km and not the orbit clip's 10 km: at that event's surge (hundreds of metres at the faces) the
shallow-water solver's step collapsed to nothing at 130x (a face velocity of 92 km/s in the log) and the
record ended on a dry shore. The 10 km surge at 30x is impact_newburyport.json; the solver's stability under
a surge far taller than its water is the open item (docs/WATER_V2.md 13.5).
Record:  build in\gagame.exe scenes\demos\impact_descent.json --mp4 outeview\impact\impact_descent.mp4
